Retrieved via Exa search highlights. Approved domain: aljazeera.com (Kyiv Post/Interfax/RBC used for cross-reference context only).

- On Thursday 16 July 2026, Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada approved Serhiy Koretsky (former CEO of state energy company Naftogaz) as the new PRIME MINISTER; 289 lawmakers backed his appointment. Nominated by President Zelensky.
- Part of a broader reshuffle triggered by the resignation of former PM Yulia Svyrydenko (parliament voted Tuesday 14 July to dismiss her, automatically dissolving the Cabinet). Svyrydenko had been PM about a year, succeeding Denys Shmyhal.
- Zelensky replaced Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov; Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko widely expected to become next defence minister. A key stated reason: Fedorov's conflict with Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrsky.
- Shmyhal reappointed as First Deputy PM and Energy Minister. FM Andrii Sybiha expected to remain.
- Al Jazeera (12 July), Zelensky on social media (DIRECT QUOTE): "Ukraine is changing its political strategy. Each priority foreign policy direction will be overseen by a specific individual with substantial experience who is capable of delivering on the agreements reached at the leaders' level and fulfilling the expectations of the Ukrainian people."
- Zelensky said the new strategy focuses on licensed manufacture of Patriot air defence systems, advancing EU membership, and deepening ties with the Gulf region.
- Svyrydenko reportedly lined up to become Ukraine's next ambassador to the US.
